$comment: Community counter database for Mechabellum. Baseline adapted from the unit guides at https://mechamonarch.com/unit/. Edit this file via PR to improve the data — see CONTRIBUTING.md. strength: 1 = soft counter, 2 = good counter (default), 3 = hard counter.

units.name: Arclight
units.description: Durable ranged ground unit with a splash cannon that is the standard chaff-clear tool, staying strong against Crawlers throughout the entire game. With Charged Shot it also punishes medium-unit pushes.

counters.reason: Splash shots wipe Crawler packs in every phase of the game
Clears them early game, though shielded Fangs later blunt its damage
Charged Shot tech lets it burst down medium armored pushes
Charged Shot deletes Steel Balls before they drill through your line
Splash damage punishes tightly packed light vehicles
AoE cannon efficiently clears cheap ground chaff

counteredBy.reason: Outranges and picks off Arclights with high single-target damage
Long-range rocket barrages destroy them before they contribute
Charges through the chaff screen and crushes them in melee
Arclight has no anti-air and dies helplessly to air attacks
Flies over the line and snipes Arclights, which cannot shoot back
Air unit it cannot target, free to beam it down
Too much HP and damage for Arclight's modest single-target output
Outranges and out-damages it with heavy siege fire

tips: Buy Range Enhancement early so Arclights stay back and don't die before finishing their job of clearing enemy chaff.
Pair Arclights with Stormcallers — Stormcallers are good against everything Arclights are weak to.
Don't build Arclights into Fangs once shield tech is on the table; they're a Crawler answer. And don't tech Anti-Aircraft — build dedicated anti-air like Mustangs instead.
Charged Shot (300) is the pickup against Steel Ball/Sledgehammer pushes; Armor Enhancement (150) is worth it when they're holding a flank.

units.name: Crawler
units.description: Cheap, extremely fast melee swarm unit and arguably the most versatile unit in the game. Used for early pressure, flanking, distracting enemy fire, and as a late-game carry with aggressive tech builds.

counters.reason: Swarms and overwhelms fragile ranged chaff before it can deal meaningful damage
Fast melee rush closes distance and shreds slow-firing single-target snipers
Reaches and destroys the fragile Hacker before it can convert valuable targets
Melting Point's slow-ramping beam can't handle dozens of small fast bodies
Mass of cheap bodies harasses and overwhelms the single-target drill damage
Fast flanking Crawlers reach the fragile artillery before rockets can thin them out
Slow single-target siege unit gets swarmed and torn down by sheer numbers
Chaff pins the worm in place and prevents its burrow cycles

counteredBy.reason: Standard early-game counter; splash cannon wipes out whole packs of Crawlers
Flamethrower area damage incinerates entire swarms almost instantly
Fire and burn damage melts massed light units
Durable splash-damage tank that absorbs the swarm and clears it efficiently
Multi-target attacks mean the swarm cannot block or soak the Wraith's damage
Rapid multi-hit area fire chews through large numbers of cheap units
Area damage and sturdy frame handle massed Crawlers well

tips: Put tanky units like Sledgehammers or Steel Balls in front so Crawlers reach the enemy without eating counter-fire, or flank from the sides — even backline Crawlers reach combat quickly.
Replicate (250) is one of the best techs in the game, but don't buy it before your free-unit card drops or you risk getting hard countered while over-committed.
Impact Drill wins Crawler mirror/replicate wars and cracks leveled towers; Mechanical Rage is the go-to final carry tech.
Drip-feed Crawlers into the fight to screen your high-value units, and sell isolated stragglers so an enemy with Replicate can't farm them for free units.

units.name: Fang
units.description: Cheap ranged chaff squad whose main job is to distract enemy fire and screen valuable units. With Portable Shield tech they become extremely durable damage sponges that can lock down slow single-target attackers.

counters.reason: Shielded Fangs lock down slow single-target damage dealers, which get stuck on them for ages
Once shielded, Fangs absorb Arclight shots and outlast its splash damage
Ignite tech and massed cheap bodies whittle down giants while soaking their expensive shots
A wall of shielded Fangs stalls the charge and buys time for your damage dealers
Cheap anti-air chaff punishes over-teched or over-built Phoenixes early
Cheap massed anti-air chaff trades very efficiently against them

counteredBy.reason: Faster melee swarm closes in and shreds Fangs in the early game
High rate-of-fire packs, especially with High-Explosive Ammo, mow Fangs down
Rocket barrages splash whole Fang squads off the board
Flame area damage burns through even shielded Fangs
Sustained multi-target fire clears massed Fangs efficiently
Area damage handles large groups of cheap infantry

tips: Build Fangs early if you plan to buy Portable Shield (their key tech) — the shield doubles their effective HP and gives huge late-game value as a screen.
Their slow movement is actually a feature: they naturally stay in front of your critical units and protect them, so position them ahead of your carries.
Avoid carry-Fang builds — Range Enhancement and Armor-Piercing Bullets are traps; Fangs are a utility/screening unit, not a damage carry.
Ignite is a strong pickup against giant-heavy boards, and Mechanical Rage works with Fortress fang-summoning synergies.

units.name: Hound
units.description: Cheap, quick ground unit that clears enemy chaff and provides extra bodies to soak damage, helping your bigger units connect faster. Levels well and can outgrow its support role to threaten medium units.

counters.reason: Efficiently guns down light melee swarms before they reach your line
Quickly clears cheap ranged chaff and screens your carries from it

counteredBy.reason: One of the best answers to Hound aggression; flame AoE wipes packs instantly
Top counter to aggressive Hound play thanks to multi-target beam damage
Fire area damage burns down massed cheap units
Sustained multi-hit fire shreds groups of Hounds
Charges through and crushes light units on impact
Devours cheap ground chaff wholesale

tips: Deploy Hounds early even without tech — they level fast, and with levels they break out of the chaff role and start clearing bigger units.
Tech priority: Range Enhancement first, then Mechanical Rage for attack speed; Fire Extinguisher (200) is a cheap defensive buy that protects nearby allies from burn damage.
They pair excellently with Overlords, Raidens, and War Factories as the screening/chaff-clear component of a premium late-game composition.
Don't rely on Incendiary Bomb early — a single anti-missile device stops a Hound from igniting its oil, neutering the tech.

units.name: Fire Badger
units.description: A cheap flamethrower tank that soaks damage on the frontline and demolishes chaff with cone-shaped fire. Plays like a Sledgehammer that trades single-target punch for anti-swarm burn.

counters.reason: Flame cone absolutely demolishes crawler swarms without needing any tech
Burns down Fang clusters, though Range Enhancement helps it connect first
With positioning and range tech it can roast Mustang packs

counteredBy.reason: Outranges the very short-ranged Badger and kills it before it fires
Too much HP for fire damage to matter and crushes Badgers up close
Charges through the flames and smashes the Badger in melee
Heavy ranged strikes from a unit the Badger cannot answer
Deletes medium flame units from beyond their effective range
Strong air matchup against medium flame units that struggle to hit air
Tanks the flames and wins the head-on trade

tips: Field Maintenance (+30% HP and regen) is its best tech — it turns the Badger into a real damage soaker.
Use it as a flanker when the enemy stacks units in a corner; the fire cone hits everything bunched together.
Its range is terrible — buy Range Enhancement if the enemy kites, and skip Ignite (low practical value).
Scorching Fire (+125% attack) lets it threaten medium units, not just chaff.

units.name: Marksman
units.description: Long-range sniper that deletes medium and large single targets, dominating passive range-war openings. Strong in the early-to-mid game but falls off as a primary late-game carry.

counters.reason: One high-damage shot swats fragile air units, especially with Aerial Specialization
Long-range high-damage shots punish big expensive air
Snipes the flame tank from far outside its short range
Outranges and out-damages it in the poke war
High single-shot damage cracks medium armor efficiently
Kills the balls at range before they ever reach your line
High single-target range damage, especially with Aerial Specialization, deletes Wraiths
Cheap long-range single-target damage picks off the expensive Raiden efficiently
High single-shot damage ignores the value of armor; a few Marksmen handle early Phantom Rays
Snipes the fragile beam platform from long range
High single-target damage picks the big frame apart from range
Outranges the very short-ranged Badger and kills it before it fires

counteredBy.reason: Swarm closes in fast and slow-firing snipers can't thin it out
Massed cheap bodies waste its expensive single-target shots
Two early Stormcallers can neutralize Marksmen with rocket splash
Air swarm dives them and each shot only kills one cheap Wasp
Flank charges reach the backline and crush the fragile snipers
Too much bulk to snipe down while it advances and spawns chaff
Untargetable while burrowed, so single-shot snipers waste their damage

tips: Only build Marksmen early when your cards justify it — you cannot transition into them late game; at that point Phoenix is the better buy.
Cap at 4-5 Marksmen; beyond that effectiveness plateaus and the mass becomes exploitable by flanks and swarms.
Range Enhancement is the first tech in about 90% of games, then Elite Marksman for scaling; take Aerial Specialization for a dedicated anti-air build.
Always screen them with chaff — an unprotected Marksman line folds instantly to Crawler swarms or a Rhino flank.

units.name: Mustang
units.description: Fast, versatile pack of light vehicles with rapid ranged fire that doubles as anti-air. A solid all-rounder that covers flanks early and scales into a late-game threat with levels and items.

counters.reason: High rate of fire mows down cheap infantry squads
Explosive Ammo and rapid fire clear melee swarms before they connect
Cheap, reliable anti-air that shreds squishy air swarms early
Massed anti-air fire brings down fragile fliers cost-efficiently
With Aerial Specialization, massed Mustangs melt big air units

counteredBy.reason: Splash damage wipes whole Mustang packs at range
Armor tech negates Mustang's low per-shot damage almost entirely
Long-range rocket splash lands on clustered Mustang packs
Tanky flame unit absorbs their fire and burns the pack down
Big armored unit shrugs off small-arms fire and locks Mustangs down
Charges into the pack and crushes it while soaking the shots
Burn AoE counters massed light vehicles
Out-trades them with multi-target sustained area fire
Cheap Armor Enhancement makes it a great answer to Mustang-heavy boards
Armor technology absorbs rapid low-damage shots, making Mustang volleys nearly useless

tips: Deploy Mustangs on your flanks even when pushing centrally — their speed lets them cover side attacks and provide constant anti-air coverage.
Range Enhancement (300) is the essential first tech for survivability and faster leveling; add Armor-Piercing Bullets for late-game armor matchups and Aerial Specialization when facing 3+ air units.
Cap your investment at roughly 3-4 packs — over-committing makes you a liability once the opponent techs armor, shields, or big units.
Pair them with Hackers, Fortresses, Steel Balls, or Rhinos to give them a frontline; naked Mustang masses fold to armor tech.

units.name: Sledgehammer
units.description: Cheap armored tank with splash cannon fire that serves as the early-game chaff clearer and a frontline damage sponge for bigger units later. Excellent value that stays relevant all game in a support role.

counters.reason: Splash shots and armor make it very good versus Crawlers all game
AoE fire clears unshielded Fang squads efficiently
With Armor Enhancement tech it nullifies Mustang damage almost completely
With missile interception it walls out Stormcaller damage

counteredBy.reason: High-damage sniper shots crack its armor from long range
Heavy siege damage deletes medium armor
Out-tanks and out-damages it in the frontline brawl
Heavy air attacks it cannot answer
Air sniper picks off Sledgehammers with impunity
Converts the cheap frontline into an enemy asset
Charge damage smashes through medium armor
Giant output overwhelms its modest DPS and HP
Damage Sharing tech plus the ramping beam melts sledge lines
High per-bolt damage one-shots medium units, hitting three targets at once
Good sustained damage against medium units that cannot shoot back at air

tips: Often correct NOT to level Sledgehammers — level 1 sledges clear chaff nearly as well, and counters overkill them anyway, so spend the supply elsewhere.
Tech priority is roughly: Field Maintenance most games, Armor Enhancement against Mustang/light-fire boards, and almost never Damage Sharing or carry techs.
Avoid carry-sledge builds (Range/EMP/Mech Rage) — they're easily shut down; keep Sledgehammers in the chaff-clear and frontline-tank role.
Against Steel Balls, deploy sledges vertically in a column so all the balls waste time drilling the first sledge; beware shielded Fangs, which sledges get stuck on forever.

units.name: Steel Ball
units.description: A durable anti-giant brawler that rolls up to big targets and melts them with a close-range beam. Works as a reactive frontline pick that tanks for backline damage dealers and snowballs hard once leveled with items.

counters.reason: The hard counter — tanks the beam while Energy Absorption feeds off it
Shreds large high-HP units at close range
The standard defensive answer — tanks the charge and melts the Rhino
Ignores chaff-clearing damage profile and burns it down up close
Excellent single-target beam damage against the biggest giant
Tanks through the Typhoon's fire and is very good against its Barrier tech
Tanky enough to shrug off flame damage while killing it

counteredBy.reason: The most universal answer; early Scorpion drops stop Steel Balls from leveling
Swarms overwhelm its slow single-target attack
Converts the slow, expensive ball into your problem
Flies over it and picks it off from range
Heavy air damage it cannot answer
Long-range missile barrages hit it before it reaches anything
Long-range lightning kills Steel Balls before they can roll into your lines
Kills Steel Balls before they reach your front line
High damage-per-shot brings balls down before they ramp

tips: Avoid Steel Balls as opening units — free Scorpion drops punish them early; deploy them as a reaction to enemy giants instead.
Mechanical Division (350) is the must-have tech — the crawlers spawned on death add chaff and pressure; Energy Absorption (200) is great versus giants and barriers.
Level them and give them items — a leveled, itemized Steel Ball frontline is extremely hard to remove; pair with Photon Overlords for extra durability.
Watch for vertical Fang walls, Charged Shot Arclights and sentry missiles — opponents use these to gather and stall your balls before they connect.

units.name: Stormcaller
units.description: A fragile long-range rocket artillery unit that saturates an area with missiles. Among the best units when unopposed — it deletes low-HP squads, stationary units and shields from far behind the frontline.

counters.reason: Low-HP squads get melted by missile volleys
Fragile squad units die to the AoE barrage
Slow-moving squads get pounded before they close the distance
Stationary backline units are easy targets for long-range missiles
Slow units can't dodge the barrage and get chipped down

counteredBy.reason: Cheap chaff absorbs missiles and rushes the fragile launchers
Jumps or flies over the frontline and kills the launchers directly
Closes in from the air and deletes the fragile artillery
Charges through the frontline and tramples the launchers
Missile Interceptor tech shoots the volleys out of the sky
Missile interception and huge HP make barrages nearly useless
Burrows under artillery barrages and Sandstorm blunts long-range damage
Outranges and snipes fragile artillery in the backline
Flies over the front line and destroys fragile artillery
Its durability shrugs off missiles while it closes in and destroys the artillery line

tips: 2-4 packs early is fine, but don't over-commit — avoid heavy levels or items on them, since anti-missile tech turns the investment into dead supply.
High-Explosive Ammo (200) is the cheap chaff-clear upgrade to buy first; Electromagnetic Explosion (300) is strong versus War Factory and Melting Point.
Never buy Armor-Piercing Bullets — it makes your missiles easier to intercept for no real gain.
Don't rely on Stormcallers as your only chaff clear late game; missile interceptor devices and interception tech will blank your whole damage output.

units.name: Wasp
units.description: Cheap, squishy air swarm that punishes boards lacking anti-air and is the perfect counter to mass Overlord or Wraith strategies. Extremely flexible harasser and flank defender that scales well into the late game.

counters.reason: Ignores ground lines and dives leveled Marksmen that lack anti-air support
Free damage onto expensive ground giants that often can't shoot back
Swarm of anti-air attacks is the classic answer to mass Overlord
With Aerial Specialization and range, Wasps out-trade Wraith strategies
Attacks from the air while the Vulcan's flames can't reach them
Aerial Specialization lets massed Wasps win the air-to-air fight
Air swarms attack from above where its ground-focused attacks have little answer

counteredBy.reason: The premier early anti-air; rapid fire shreds squishy Wasps
With Anti-Air Barrage it fends off Wasps while also tanking the front
Cheap massed anti-air chaff trades very efficiently against them
Multi-target air-to-air damage clears Wasp swarms if they lack range/aerial tech
Sustained multi-target flak chews through the swarm
Clears fragile air swarms while tanking their damage
Its anti-air output clears Wasp swarms efficiently

tips: Buy Jump Drive (50) almost always as the first upgrade — repositioning between rounds keeps Wasps unpredictable and lets them defend a flank then rejoin the main fight.
Aerial Specialization (200) is mandatory before committing into Wasps when the opponent has air; Range Enhancement (300) is required for carry builds but buying it too early telegraphs your plan.
Use them as flank defenders and harassers targeting gaps in the enemy line; clever placement can even tank sentry-missile splash to protect ground units behind them.
Don't rely on Energy Shield to fix their squishiness — opponents just build Mustangs and the shield barely matters.

units.name: Farseer
units.description: A flexible do-it-all flying giant that provides mid-game power, decent chaff clear, and anti-air, while its EMP shuts down key enemy units. Strong in rounds 3-5 but falls off against dedicated late-game units.

counters.reason: Its anti-air output clears Wasp swarms efficiently
Can shoot down and EMP-disable enemy Wraiths
Good damage against clustered medium ground units
Kills Steel Balls before they reach your front line
Protects you from Overlord rush cheese by contesting the air early

counteredBy.reason: Too much health for the Farseer's damage to handle as the game goes on
Charges through to the backline where Farseer's damage cannot stop it
Massive durable giant that Farseer cannot meaningfully damage
Ramping beam damage destroys expensive flying giants

tips: Build only 1-2 Farseers as a mid-game power spike; massing them loses to better units later in the game.
Skip range technology on it; the tech investment creates a resource disadvantage.
EMP tech is cheap and sometimes worth it to disable enemy Vulcans, Wraiths, or Melting Points when pushing.
Use it as insurance against random cheese plays like Overlord rushes rather than as a long-term carry.

units.name: Hacker
units.description: A support unit that converts enemy units to your side. High-risk, high-reward: it either steals something expensive or continuously steals small units that distract the opponent's whole army.

counters.reason: Hacking a leveled ball flips the tempo, but you need a same-level Hacker to hack reliably
Cheap medium units are hacked quickly and clog the enemy push
Hacks the charging unit early and turns it around, controlling its aggression
Gets distracted by hacked units and just spins around instead of dealing damage
Wastes its ramping beam retargeting hacked chaff
Too slow at clearing hacked units, so the distraction keeps working
One hack steals a large, expensive frontliner

counteredBy.reason: Cheap swarms reach and kill the fragile Hacker; hacking one Crawler barely matters
Chaff overwhelms it and each hack steals almost no value
Long-range barrages kill the fragile Hacker before it pays off
Fast chaff clear kills hacked units before they distract anything
Instantly burns down hacked chaff, nullifying the distraction plan
Barrier tech and heavy fire shut the Hacker down
Shielded and too valuable to trade into; produces chaff that screens it
Multi-target damage clears hacked units and threatens the Hacker itself
Kills Hackers while armor mitigates incoming damage

tips: Buy Range Enhancement (300) almost always — it lets the Hacker sit safely behind your army and survive.
Barriers hard-counter hacking; pair Hackers with shield-breakers like Stormcallers and answer enemy barrier tech early.
Don't pair Hackers with strong single-target damage — your own Marksmen or Phoenixes will kill the target before the hack completes.
Multiple Control (250) is only good against chaff boards; it fails against high-level units. Late game, kill your own hacked units quickly before the enemy reclaims value.

units.name: Phantom Ray
units.description: A durable flying unit that serves as the frontline for your air army. With armor technology it blanks rapid-fire units while dealing good damage to medium-sized ground units.

counters.reason: Armor technology absorbs rapid low-damage shots, making Mustang volleys nearly useless
Good sustained damage against medium units that cannot shoot back at air
Attacks from the air while taking little in return from medium units
Flies over the front line and destroys fragile artillery
Kills Hackers while armor mitigates incoming damage
Strong matchup against medium flame units that struggle to hit air
Trades favorably as an armored air frontliner against enemy air

counteredBy.reason: High single-shot damage ignores the value of armor; a few Marksmen deal with early Phantom Rays
Big single-target hits punch straight through armor
Massed Overlords and anti-air overwhelm multiple Phantom Rays
Ramping beam (especially with Energy Absorption) melts armored air units
High-damage lightning bolts are not mitigated well by armor
Anti-air giant that contests it directly in the air

tips: Buy it primarily to counter enemy Mustang masses, taking armor technology first.
After armor wins that fight, add shield technology to defend against the Phoenix and Marksman response.
Avoid overcommitting to fast-shooting units yourself early, or you invite the same armor-based counter.
If facing enemy Phantom Rays, respond with a few Marksmen or Phoenixes early, or Energy Absorption Melting Points and missile-interceptor Mustangs later.

units.name: Phoenix
units.description: A mobile air unit (2 per pack) firing high single-target damage shots, excellent at early harassment and flanking. With Jump Drive it teleports across the board to assassinate artillery and giants in the enemy backline.

counters.reason: Flies or jumps past the frontline and kills the fragile launchers
Ground-only unit that can't shoot back at air
Big ground target with no anti-air answer
Charged Shot deletes it and it can't retaliate against air
High single-target damage picks off expensive air giants
No anti-air, so Phoenixes kill it for free
Instantly connects to big backline units and bursts them down
Repositions to focus down the big single target
Ground unit with no way to hit air
Charged Shot Phoenixes burst the big air target down
Charged shot deals enough burst to kill it during its surface window
Air sniper picks off Sledgehammers with impunity
Flies over it and picks it off from range
Big single-target hits punch straight through armor
Air-to-air single-target damage trades very well against it
High single-target air damage strikes it while staying hard for it to answer
Snipes the fragile beam platform while flying out of its reach
Air harassment it has no good response to

counteredBy.reason: Massed anti-air fire shreds the fragile pairs
Cheap anti-air chaff punishes over-teched or over-built Phoenixes early
Long-range single-target shots two-tap Phoenixes
Swarming air-to-air unit that trades up against them
Anti-Air Barrage connects to Phoenixes even with units in front

tips: Jump Drive (50) is the best Phoenix tech — buy it almost always and use aggressive flank placements to reach the enemy backline.
Electromagnetic Shot (200) guarantees hits and locks down Fortresses and Melting Points; Charged Shot (200) is great versus shields, Rhinos and Wraiths.
Don't overcommit early — if you tech too fast or build too many, cheap anti-air like Fangs and Mustangs punishes you hard.
Prefer aggressive positioning over Range Enhancement, but place short-range builds carefully so they don't fly into massed anti-air.

units.name: Raiden
units.description: A flying backline carry, often described as a flying Scorpion, that fires three lightning bolts at long range. It struggles early but scales hard with levels, range, and items against medium-unit compositions.

counters.reason: Its high per-bolt damage one-shots medium units, hitting three targets at once
Long-range lightning kills Steel Balls before they can roll into your lines
Outranges and snipes fragile artillery in the backline
Deletes medium flame units from beyond their effective range

counteredBy.reason: Cheap long-range single-target damage picks off the expensive Raiden efficiently
Air-to-air single-target damage trades very well against it
Heavy anti-air firepower punishes a Raiden-based backline
Anti-air capable giant that can EMP and shoot it down
Ramping beam damage burns through the costly giant

tips: Buy Raiden only after the opponent has overcommitted to medium units; it struggles heavily against chaff early on.
Prioritize Range Enhancement first for both safety and damage uptime.
Add Chain tech to arc onto backline counters, and consider Electromagnetic Shot late to disable counters once range and chain are in place.
Protect it with chaff clear elsewhere on the board, since it cannot efficiently clear Crawlers and Fangs on its own.

units.name: Rhino
units.description: A fast melee bruiser that must be played aggressively: it charges the enemy line, draws fire for your damage dealers, and threatens towers via multi-directional flanks and mobile beacons.

counters.reason: Charges through and tramples the fragile artillery
Runs it down before its chip damage matters
Closes distance fast and kills the big chaff-clearer in melee
Whirlwind tech is insane against multi-unit squads
Whirlwind AoE shreds squad-based medium units
Reaches the backline and crushes stationary snipers
Whirlwind clears the fragile squads on contact
Tanks the flame damage and kills it up close
Gets on top of it quickly and out-brawls it
Charges through and crushes light units on impact
Charges through to the backline where Farseer's damage cannot stop it

counteredBy.reason: The standard defensive answer — tanks the charge and melts the Rhino
Ramping beam kills the charging Rhino before it does its job
Too tanky to trample and hits back extremely hard
Hacks the Rhino early and turns your aggression against you
Charged Shot Phoenixes burst it down while staying untouchable in the air
Kites the melee charger from the air
Shoots in all directions, walling off Rhino flanks

tips: Deploy Rhinos in front of your damage dealers to soak aggro, or on wide flanks with a mobile beacon to hunt towers.
Whirlwind (250) is the go-to tech versus chaff; Power Armor (300) negates slows and is essential for tower rushes; Photon Coating (300) gives strong early damage reduction.
Against Final Blitz Rhinos, don't cluster your units — spread deployments so one death explosion can't chain through your army.
Don't over-rely on Armor Enhancement — opponents simply answer with Steel Balls or Melting Points; scout where enemy defenses are thin instead.

units.name: Abyss
units.description: A late-game ground giant that devastates clustered ground armies with heavy area attacks. Its huge health pool and splash damage make it a powerful anchor, but it is slow and expensive.

counters.reason: Area damage wipes out chaff swarms that try to surround it
Splash attacks clear massed cheap infantry instantly
Heavy area damage crushes clumped medium ground units
Its durability shrugs off missiles while it closes in and destroys the artillery line

counteredBy.reason: Ramping beam damage is the premier answer to any high-health giant
Air units with high single-target damage strike it while staying hard for it to answer
Air swarms attack from above where its ground-focused attacks have little answer
Flying giant that can chip it down and EMP-disable it from the air

tips: Treat it as a late-game investment like other 400-cost giants; deploying it too early cripples your economy.
Aim it at the enemy's densest ground clumps so its area damage hits as many units as possible.
Expect a Melting Point response and pre-position chaff, Hackers, or EMP to protect it.
Pair it with dedicated anti-air, since air compositions are the safest way for opponents to play around it.

units.name: Sabertooth
units.description: A rare heavy tank obtained only from free unit packs. A big early-game powerhouse when leveled with an item, it anchors your frontline and, with Missile Interceptor, doubles as anti-Stormcaller defense.

counters.reason: Out-trades medium units with superior HP and firepower
High damage-per-shot brings balls down before they ramp
Missile Interceptor tech lets one Sabertooth blank roughly one Stormcaller
Tanks the flames and wins the head-on trade
Crushes medium squad units in direct engagements

counteredBy.reason: Ramping beam removes the big single tank
Bigger tank that out-trades it head-on
Air unit it can't shoot; Launcher Overload beats its missile interception
Flies over it and chips it down for free
One hack steals a large, expensive frontliner
Aggressive melee pressure it struggles to shake off
Chaff swarms overwhelm its slow, single-target shots

tips: Only build extra Sabertooths when the enemy lacks chaff clear, runs medium units, or fields 2+ Stormcallers — otherwise use the free one for early value and sell it later.
Missile Interceptor (200) is the standout tech versus Stormcallers; Doubleshot (100) creates crazy tempo against giants.
Keep it on the frontline protected by your own chaff — skip Range Enhancement, screening bodies do that job better.
Don't rely on Missile Interceptor against Overlords once they can buy Launcher Overload — it will stop working.

units.name: Sandworm
units.description: A burrowing giant that dives underground between attacks, dodging fire while dealing heavy damage when it surfaces. Excels at protecting your army with Sandstorm and disrupting long-range compositions.

counters.reason: Burrows under artillery barrages and Sandstorm blunts long-range damage
Untargetable while burrowed, so single-shot snipers waste their damage
Surfaces on top of it and its Sandstorm-covered allies survive the fire
Heavy surfacing damage chews through slow medium units
Dives under the sustained fire and crushes it on emergence
Devours cheap ground chaff wholesale

counteredBy.reason: Absolutely demolishes worms — too much HP and firepower to burrow-cycle against
Beam ramps up and burns through it whenever it surfaces
Charged shot deals enough burst to kill it during its surface window
Ground cannon volleys hit hard the moment the worm emerges
Chaff pins the worm in place and prevents its burrow cycles

tips: Sandstorm is the headline tech: 30% ranged damage reduction protects Wasps and your whole push.
Concentrate your firepower in one lane so the worm can keep burrow-cycling instead of getting pinned.
Replicate/Mechanical Division make worms snowball — larvae protect the original and multiply value.
Don't buy Anti-Air by default; the worm's job is protection and disruption, not air defense.

units.name: Scorpion
units.description: A heavy assault giant whose burst attack and acid specialize in deleting medium armor, shields, and summon-spam. The classic answer to Steel Balls and a solid early frontline tank.

counters.reason: Its best use case — burst damage one-shots Steel Balls before they close in
Heavy volleys smash medium armor lines efficiently
Clears all the summons while acid attack eats the factory itself
Acid and heavy hits punish barriers and big HP pools (though it's not a hard counter)

counteredBy.reason: The Scorpion's biggest counter — flies, outranges it, and it can't answer air
Cheap chaff distracts and surrounds it; its slow burst overkills 100-cost units
Snipes it from beyond its reach

Artillery pounds the slow giant from far outside its range
Instantly connects to big backline units and bursts them down
Gets distracted by hacked units and just spins around instead of dealing damage

tips: Always pair Scorpions with chaff clear (Vulcan or Mustangs) — alone they get swarmed by Crawlers.
Start with a single Scorpion as an early frontline tank; only mass them once you have Range/Acid tech.
Field Maintenance is the best survivability tech; Acid Attack scales hard into late game.
Don't buy Range Enhancement too early — it invites the opponent to pivot into Overlords.

units.name: Tarantula
units.description: A tanky multi-legged frontliner that clears chaff very well early game and deals decent damage to medium units. Best used as a solid, low-investment early-game wall rather than a scaling core unit.

Multi-shot attacks and high HP dominate swarm boards
Cheap Armor Enhancement makes it a great answer to Mustang-heavy boards

Deals solid damage against medium squad units
Out-tanks and out-damages it in direct trades

tips: Use Tarantulas as a solid early-game frontline and generally don't build more or tech them — they fall off against giants.
If you do commit, Spider Mine (300) is the best tech and its real power spike — mines add chaff and distract enemy heavy hitters.
Armor Enhancement (200) is a cheap, efficient buy specifically against Mustang-heavy opponents.
Always deploy them at the front to get full value from their HP; pairing with Jump Drive Wasps makes for a strong combined push.

units.name: Typhoon
units.description: A medium frontline unit (deployed in pairs) that hoses down swarms with rapid multi-barrel fire — essentially a bigger Mustang that shreds chaff instead of big units. Works as an aggressive pusher or as a defender against enemy aggression.

Clears massed Fangs quickly with sustained volume of fire
Strong anti-air volume of fire, especially with Aerial Specialization
Out-trades Mustang packs in sustained damage exchanges
Sustained multi-hit fire shreds groups of Hounds

Gets on top of it quickly and out-brawls it
Dives under the sustained fire and crushes it on emergence

tips: Deploy Typhoons vertically (one behind the other) so both benefit from Barrier and they arrive in waves.

It has no range tech — use it up front as an aggressive unit or to defend against pushes, not as backline DPS.
Don't send Typhoons into medium/heavy armor lines — they kill chaff, not tanks.

units.name: War Factory
units.description: A massive late-game ground giant that acts as a mobile production facility and powerful missile interceptor. It shuts down missile-based compositions while spawning units that match its own level.

Massive durable giant that Farseer cannot meaningfully damage

Ramping beam damage is ideal against a single enormous target

tips: Do not deploy it before round 5; the 200-per-round upkeep (100 with Efficient Maintenance) is too heavy for the early economy.
Use it primarily as an anti-missile deterrent rather than a summoning factory; that is where most of its value comes from.
Screen it with shielded Fangs to bait enemy fire before it arrives, and consider range tech to keep it out of danger.
Remember it cannot equip items, and its spawned units inherit its level, so leveling it improves the whole package.

units.name: Wraith
units.description: A large flying platform that hits many targets at once, making it a premier chaff-clearer whose damage can't be body-blocked. Strong played aggressively on flanks or defensively against swarm-based aggression.

counters.reason: Multi-target beams hit the whole swarm; damage can't be blocked by bodies

tips: Range Enhancement (300) is essentially mandatory and should be bought early — without it Wraiths drift too far forward and die.
Degenerate Beam (200) adds a strong slow/weaken effect, but watch for Photon Coating which negates it.
Wraiths love items — all damage and HP items synergize; Floating Artillery Array (400) doubles output if you commit to mass Wraith.
Use them as your answer to clustered aggressive chaff, and avoid clustering your own units under enemy Wraiths.

units.name: Fortress
units.description: A hugely versatile frontline giant that tanks, clears medium units, and covers the sky with Anti-Air Barrage. Can be leveled as a carry, massed cheaply, or used as a Fang-summoning factory.

Barrier also blocks acid, EMP, and battlefield spells — it's defensive tech against far more than damage.
Fang Summoning feeds bodies to enemy single-target carries (Melting Point, Marksman) so your giants survive longer.

units.description: A backline beam giant whose damage ramps up the longer it stays on one target, making it the game's premier giant-killer. Useless against swarms, devastating against anything big.

units.name: Vulcan
units.description: A giant flamethrower platform that clears everything small — the premier anti-chaff unit in the game. Bring it when the enemy's crawlers, fangs, or mustangs are bunched where its fire can reach them.

Always pair it with single-target damage (Melting Point, Marksman, Phoenix, Overlord) — the Vulcan only handles the small stuff.

generalTips.tip: Skip the reinforcement card in rounds 2 and 3 most of the time to bank the 50 supply, unless you are offered a top-tier card that changes your whole game plan.
Don't waste extra supply just because you have it; saving for an impactful turn beats reckless spending — the economy rewards smart spending over expansion for its own sake.
Pick economy-oriented specialists (Deployment, Supply, Junior Recruitment) early so your income scales into the mid-game.
Vary your strategy based on the cards you are offered each round instead of forcing a fixed build; the offered cards should shape your game plan.
Avoid picking expensive cards like Lightning Storm or Nuke too early; winning early rounds matters less than building economy and board strength.
Never hold items in your inventory; equip them immediately (for example on flankers) — unused items are a significant tempo loss.
Victory is determined by which units are deployed against which units, not raw stats — position and matchup beat pure power.
Cover your flanks early with cheap units like Crawlers and Fangs; protecting the edges of your army enables stronger plays on later turns.
Don't neglect the tower-side lane; overcommitting elsewhere while leaving it open is a common way to lose games.
Use Intensive Training and unit levels on mid-tier units like Mustangs, Sledgehammers, and Hackers; leveling giants commits too many resources and under-develops your board.
Avoid over-committing to a single unit type; keep board balance so one enemy counter cannot invalidate your whole army.
Supply Specialist (+50 supply per round with no drawback) is the easiest and best starting specialist for new players; Quick Supply (200 supply in round one) is a flexible alternative.
Choose your starting specialist based on your starting unit combination and the opponent's composition rather than treating tier lists as absolute law.
Don't build reactive counters like Melting Point automatically; first assess whether the matchup actually justifies the investment.
When selling a leveled unit that carries an item, reclaim the item first so you can reuse it on giants or other key units instead of losing its value.
